labels.label: T-abs-gh-without-tarentin/1-arcs
labels.notes: arcCausality γ (scaffold/CausalScaffold/GHWithoutTarentin.lean:124) is a library Causal.Causality (Causal/Causality.lean:77). Every field of Precausality and Causality is discharged and the kernel accepts the structure. le U x y := (x ∈ U ∧ x = y) ∨ TransGen (arcStep γ U) x y, where arcStep (:103) is one step along one arc γ i, with 0 ≤ s ≤ t ≤ 1 and γ i '' [s, t] ⊆ U. lt := False. ≪ empty is allowed: it is open, transitive and inside ≤, and ETT's own lightlike line has it (ex:causalities_lines). Causal arc-connectedness (:189) holds for any continuous arcs. A step is its arc reparametrised (CurveOn.comp_affine, Causal/Curves.lean:209). A chain is the concatenation (CurveOn.exists_concat, Causal/ArcConnected.lean:96). The lt half is vacuous. AbsolutelyMinimal follows by CausallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimal (ArcConnected.lean:216). AbsolutelyMinimalOn W for every W follows by CausallyArcConnectedOn.absolutelyMinimalOn (:203); #print shows it quantifies over every cover S of W and every V ≤ W, which is the either-reading form of kb/0074. ArcCoherent (:235) is not vacuous. With i = j it forces each arc to be injective on [0, 1]. For i ≠ j it forces two arcs through one point to share the parameter and the past. Both models discharge it, and the fork exercises the overlap clause (the common segment [a, w], the common start b). ArcCoherent.le_iff (:258) is the evidence's one-path form. isCausal: x ≤ y ≤ x forces equal parameters. diamond_eq_image gives J_M(γ s, γ t) = γ '' [s, t], so a diamond is empty, a point or a compact arc piece. That gives CausallyCompact and GloballyHyperbolic = IsCausal ∧ CausallyCompact, matching #print and def:globally_hyperbolic (ETT.tex:995-996). The criteria are correct. causallyConvexIn: a set convex along every arc is CausallyConvexIn V ⊤, through mem_diamond. hasTimeFunction: a continuous T strictly increasing along every arc on [0, 1] gives HasTimeFunction. Push-up and ¬ chronal neighbours are vacuous because ≪ is empty, and the docstring says so.

labels.label: T-abs-gh-without-tarentin/2-fork
labels.notes: The coordinates are a = (0,0), w = (1/2,1), x_n = (1, 1+ε_n), b = (1,1), y_n = (0, −ε_n), with ε_n = 1/(n+1). I re-derived the incidences. [a, w] is y = 2x and [b, y_n] is y = x(1+ε_n) − ε_n; they would meet only at x < 0. [w, x_n] lies at y ≥ 1, with equality only at w. [b, y_m] lies at y ≤ 1, with equality only at b. So the inl and inr families are disjoint (forkArc_inl_ne_inr). x_n → b and y_n → a. The limit segments are [w, b] (y = 1) and [b, a] (y = x), and each meets the fork only at its ends. This is the sketch's combinatorics and local picture; homeomorphy is argued in SCOPE, and the title does not ask for it. The change of coordinates is disclosed in SCOPE and in the REPORT row. The carrier is a subtype of ℝ × ℝ, so T2Space and SecondCountableTopology come from mathlib instances and are conjoined in fork_separates. GH comes from 1-arcs. StronglyCausalOpen (:589) is exactly #print's ∀ p, ∀ U ∈ 𝓝 p, ∃ V : Opens, p ∈ V ∧ V ⊆ U ∧ CausallyConvexIn V ⊤. Every open box is causally convex, because both coordinates are monotone along every arc (forkArc_monotone; I checked min(2t, 1+(2t−1)ε) and both inr coordinates). That is stronger than the sketch. Reading 'open convex neighbourhoods' as StronglyCausalOpen is right: defi:convexite_causale (ETT.tex:657-660) defines causal convexity of open sets, and convexity in ℝ² is meaningless for a star of segments. No time function (:664): T a < T w ≤ T b ≤ T a, by continuity along x_n → b and y_n → a, for the ladder's HasTimeFunction. ¬ Tarentin uses causal_ladder through Levin's edge read backwards. The edge is the ladder's [[implies]] globally_hyperbolic ∧ tarentin ⇒ time_function, witness Causal.Causality.GloballyHyperbolic.hasTimeFunction [T2Space] [SecondCountableTopology] (LevinTimeFunction.lean:535). Tarentin's openDiamond is interior (diamond), as in def:tarentin_spacetime, so this is not a ≪-vacuity, and a direct check at w agrees. ¬ ChronalNeighbours holds. fork_not_le_W_B, hence ¬ IsClosed J⁺(w) and ¬ IsClosed ≤_M.

labels.label: T-abs-gh-without-tarentin/3-loop-fan
labels.notes: Each tent γ_n is the graph of y = 1 + ε_n − (n+2)|x| over [−ε_n, ε_n]. Since (n+2)ε_n = 1 + ε_n (combEps_mul), it runs from p_n = (ε_n, 0) through (0, 1+ε_n) to q_n = (−ε_n, 0). The tents are disjoint: on the common domain, tent n minus tent m = ε_n − ε_m + (m−n)|x| > 0 for n < m. a = (0,0) lies on none of them (loopγ_coherent). p_n, q_n → a. The tents accumulate on {0} × [0, 1], which meets the carrier only at a, the same as the sketch's rectangles; the change is disclosed. The carrier is a subtype of ℝ × ℝ (insert (0,0) of the union). GH comes from 1-arcs. The time function is T = −x: it is continuous, and x = ε_n(1 − 2t) is strictly decreasing along each tent. That suffices for the title's 'with a time function'. loopFan_not_stronglyCausalAt (:861) takes U = {y < 1}. Every V ∈ 𝓝 a with V ⊆ U holds p_n and q_n for large n, and causal convexity would put the peak (0, 1+ε_n) ∈ J_M(p_n, q_n) in V ⊆ {y < 1}. The quantifier is over all neighbourhoods V, not only open ones. That is exactly the negation of def:strongly_causal_spacetime's clause at p = a (ETT.tex:662-665), with DEC-7's not-necessarily-open V, the weaker property, so the failure is the stronger one. It refutes the open form too, since an open V ∋ a is in 𝓝 a. So ¬ StronglyCausal, and ¬ StronglyCausalOpen through strongly_causal_open ⇒ strongly_causal. ¬ Tarentin uses causal_ladder through prop:GH_fortement_causal's edge (GloballyHyperbolic.stronglyCausal [T2Space], GlobalHyperbolicity.lean:217) read backwards. CurvesExtend comes from time_function. ¬ ChronalNeighbours holds.

labels.label: T-abs-gh-without-tarentin/4-separation
labels.notes: I read off the elaborated types the constants of fork_separates and loopFan_separates (getUsedConstants, Causal prefix). They are exactly the ladder's lean fields: Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal (via toPrecausality), and Causal.Causality.CausallyArcConnected, PushUp, LocallyPushUp, IsCausal, CausallyCompact, GloballyHyperbolic, StronglyCausalOpen, StronglyCausal, HasTimeFunction, CurvesExtend, Tarentin and ChronalNeighbours. Each was #printed and matches programme/ladder.toml's [[property]] lean and what fields. Each [[fails]] from-list of for_keeper is exactly the positive conjuncts of its witness, and each to is a negated conjunct. The three _bare theorems have the form ¬ ∀ (M : Type) [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M] (C : Causality M), C.GloballyHyperbolic → … → P. Their extra premises (StronglyCausalOpen or HasTimeFunction, and CausallyArcConnected) make each negation stronger, not weaker. Findings: (a) prop:GH_fortement_causal (ETT.tex:1199-1200) assumes a tarentin topological spacetime, that is second countable, Hausdorff and a causality (def:category_topological_spacetimes, ETT.tex:254-256), and GH. The loop fan keeps all of these, minus tarentin, in either reading, and is not strongly causal in either form: true. (b) prop:GH_Jferme (ETT.tex:1178-1180) has the same hypotheses. The fork keeps them minus tarentin, and both conclusions fail: ≤_M is not closed, and J⁺(K) is not closed for the compact K = {w}. True. It matches the library's GloballyHyperbolic.isClosed_le_and_isClosed_J and isClosed_Jplus_singleton, which both take Tarentin (GlobalHyperbolicity.lean:93, :148). (c) Levin's edge carries standing T2 and second countable, with no ETT label. The fork keeps them and GH, and has no HasTimeFunction: true. The REPORT names the notion as the ladder's, not defi:fonction_temps, so it is not overstated. I also re-derived the closer's 'argued' remark that the fork is not locally compact at b: on [w, x_n], points at a fixed abscissa accumulate on [w, b] outside the fork.

findings.what: 'Each states a conjunct of the witness and moves no pair' is true, but under the committed tool (bce2a8d) it understates the case. counterexample()'s backward reading already derives all four from the load-bearing entries. The fork's time_function entry lacks {chronal_neighbours, tarentin, time_function}, through Levin's edge read backwards and chronal_neighbours ⇒ tarentin. The loop fan's strongly_causal entry lacks {chronal_neighbours, strongly_causal, strongly_causal_open, tarentin}, through GH ∧ tarentin ⇒ strongly_causal read backwards. So the optional entries restate what the tool infers. Under the pre-bce2a8d tool they would at least have added lacks; under bce2a8d they add nothing.
